title: Complete secure GitHub sign-in and session lifecycle
description: Implement the approved GitHub identity and session flow for the real application, following the selected Git workspace architecture and least-privilege rules.
acceptanceCriteria: A user can sign in, return to the application, and see authenticated state without exposing OAuth secrets or privileged tokens to the browser.
Logout, expired/revoked sessions, denied authorization, and retry paths have clear tested behavior.
Only permissions needed for the currently implemented read workflows are requested; Git write permissions remain deferred until their feature is implemented.
The actual configured development flow is documented without exposing .env values.

steps.details: Read applicable auth/security specs and current auth code; do not assume a provider integration not selected in the specs.

steps.description: Implement the smallest secure end-to-end auth slice
steps.details: Preserve server-side credential boundaries and existing project conventions.
Add focused tests for state/session behavior and run required project checks.

technicalNotes: Do not read, print, copy, or commit .env values.
Do not request broad GitHub permissions just for future roadmap features.
